title: NSS Feed Output Format: Endpoint DLP Logs

blocks.text: The Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feed specifies the data from the Endpoint DLP logs that the NSS sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system. You can configure an NSS feed by including one or more fields. The fields and their values display in the NSS feed output.

blocks.text: The following tables display information about the Endpoint DLP log fields and possible values for those fields.

Fields that support obfuscation are documented in the following tables with the prefix o (e.g., %s{ouser}). To obfuscate a field, manually add the prefix o before the field name in the Feed Output Format in the Zscaler Admin Console.
The following are date and time fields:

table: The log time (i.e., when a transaction is logged by the Zscaler Nanolog)
The feed time (i.e., when a transaction is received by the NSS from the Nanolog)

The event time (i.e., when an event is intercepted and evaluated by the DLP service). An event (e.g., file copied to local drive) can be classified as an activity or as an incident, if it violates a DLP rule.
The time zone. This is the same as the time zone you specified when you configured the NSS feed.

blocks.text: The following are scan information fields:

table: The number of DLP engines hit
The number of DLP dictionaries hit
The scanned item (file or text) size in bytes

blocks.text: The following are user information fields:

table: The obfuscated version of the username. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the department name. This displays a random string.

blocks.text: The following are device information fields:

table: The obfuscated version of the device name. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the device owner. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the device hostname. This displays a random string.

blocks.text: The following are data center information fields:

table: The name of the data center
The city where the data center is located
The country where the data center is located

blocks.text: The following are file information fields:

table: The obfuscated version of the file source path. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the file destination path. This displays a random string.
The type of document uploaded or downloaded during the transaction
The subtype of the document uploaded or downloaded during the transaction
The obfuscated version of the item name. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the item source name. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the item destination name. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the DLP engine names. This displays a random string.
The obfuscated version of the DLP dictionary names. This displays a random string.
The number of hits for each of the DLP dictionaries
The confirmation action by the user
The action taken by Endpoint DLP

The severity of the event. An event is either an incident or a sensitive activity. An incident violates an Endpoint DLP rule and the severity (High, Medium, Low, Info) is based on the rule that was violated. A sensitive activity does not violate a rule and is reported for visibility (Info).
High Severity Medium Severity Low Severity Info Severity

The DLP rule that was triggered. An event can trigger multiple rules, out of which the DLP service applies the most restrictive rule. The applied rule is the "triggered" rule, while the other rules are stored as "other" rules (i.e., %s{otherrulelabels}).
The obfuscated version of the triggered DLP rule. This displays a random string.
The labels of other rules that were triggered. See %s{triggeredrulelabel}.
The obfuscated version of the other rule labels. This displays a random string.
The expected action by Endpoint DLP
File already open by another application
The option selected by the user to justify a transaction that triggers a DLP rule with the Confirm action

1 - User didn't provide justification in time 2 - The data contains only my personal information 3 - This activity is part of a necessary business workflow 4 - This activity was accidental 5 - The data does not contain sensitive information 6 - Other
The message entered by a user to justify a transaction that triggers a DLP rule with the Confirm action

blocks.text: A SIEM can have parsing issues whenever a string field has non-printable or delimiter characters. For that reason, the Zscaler service has URL encoding for URL fields like URL, Referer, and Hostname. There are several other fields that have the same parsing issue, but URL encoding is not suitable. Such fields are encoded using Base64.
Turning on Base64 encoding for all supported fields might result in approximately a 20% drop in performance.

The Zscaler service hex encodes all non-printable ASCII characters that are in URLs when it sends logs to the NSS. Any URL character that is less than or equal to 0x20, or greater than or equal to 0x7F, is encoded as %HH. This ensures that your SIEM can parse the URLs that contain control characters. For example, a \n character in a URL is encoded as %0A, and a space is encoded as %20.
